answer.question: Why did tofersen miss its VALOR primary endpoint, and which patients might still benefit?

claims.claim: VALOR Part C (NCT02623699) tested tofersen in SOD1-ALS.
The prespecified Part C primary endpoint was change from baseline in ALSFRS-R total score at Week 28 (Day 197).
VALOR missed its primary endpoint: the LS mean difference in ALSFRS-R change was 1.2 (95% CI -3.19 to 5.53; p=0.9689), indicating no statistically significant treatment effect.

The curated record states VALOR missed the short-duration clinical primary endpoint and that tofersen later pursued accelerated approval using plasma neurofilament light as a surrogate alongside further testing.

claims.claim: The curated record notes FDA accelerated approval in April 2023 for SOD1-ALS and clarifies this was a biomarker/regulatory strategy, not proof that post hoc clinical analysis made the original primary result positive.

claims.claim: Secondary biomarker results showed tofersen reduced CSF total SOD1 (ratio 0.62, 95% CI 0.49-0.78; p<0.0001) and plasma NfL (ratio 0.33, 95% CI 0.25-0.45; p<0.0001) at Week 28.

Other secondary clinical measures at Week 28 were not significant: HHD megascore LS mean difference 0.02 (95% CI -0.207 to 0.255; p=0.839) and percent predicted SVC LS mean difference 7.9 (95% CI -3.528 to 19.322; p=0.3233).

VALOR Part C (NCT02623699) showed a reduction in CSF total SOD1 protein concentration ratio to baseline at Week 28 (Day 197) (difference in LS geometric mean ratio 0.62, 95% CI 0.49-0.78, p<0.0001) and a reduction in plasma NfL concentration ratio to baseline at Day 197 (Week 28) (difference in LS geometric mean ratio 0.33, 95% CI 0.25-0.45, p<0.0001); the tofersen program pursued accelerated approval using plasma NfL as a surrogate, and FDA granted accelerated approval in April 2023 for SOD1-ALS.
claims.repaired_from: Patients who might still benefit are those with SOD1-ALS, based on the biomarker reductions and subsequent accelerated approval for SOD1-ALS.
